title: Percy Fawcett | The Real Life Indiana Jones
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 推出的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在节目中，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪、美妙绝伦的事物，同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about a man called Percy Fawcett.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊一个名叫 Percy Fawcett 的人。

sentences.en: You may remember this name from an episode at the start of the year on secret, lost civilisations, and if you were listening very carefully you might recall I said that this story deserved its own episode.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得今年年初有一期关于神秘失落文明的节目提到了这个名字，如果你当时听得很仔细，可能还记得我说过这个故事值得单独出一期节目。

sentences.en: And this is it, a story of adventure, exploration, discovery, fearlessness, success against all the odds, an unsolved mystery, and the story of a real-life Indiana Jones.
sentences.zh: 这就是那一期节目：这是一个关于冒险、探索、发现、无畏、历经万难终获成功、未解之谜的故事，也是一个现实版 Indiana Jones 的故事。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it and learn about the story of Percy Fawcett.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们马上切入正题，来了解 Percy Fawcett 的故事。

sentences.en: Picture the late 19th century. Most maps of the world still had large blank spaces, swathes of “uncharted territory” just waiting for someone brave enough—or reckless enough—to fill them in.
sentences.zh: 想象一下 19 世纪末。当时世界上绝大多数地图都还留有大片空白，大片“未探索的领土”正等待着足够勇敢——或者足够鲁莽——的人去填补。

sentences.en: Exploration was the ultimate frontier, and it promised fortune, glory, and the chance to write your name into history.
sentences.zh: 探索是终极的前沿，它承诺带来财富、荣耀，以及将你的名字写入历史的机会。

sentences.en: Into this era stepped Percy Harrison Fawcett: a dashing, determined British explorer with an uncanny ability to survive conditions that killed lesser men in days.
sentences.zh: 踏入这个时代的是 Percy Harrison Fawcett：一位风度翩翩、意志坚定的英国探险家，他有着不可思议的能力，能在那些让普通人几天内丧命的环境中生存下来。

sentences.en: In 1925, at the age of 58, he ventured deep into the Amazon rainforest on a quest for what he believed was a lost city—a place he called “Z.”
sentences.zh: 1925 年，58 岁的他深入亚马逊雨林，寻找他坚信存在的一座失落之城——一个他称之为“Z”的地方。

sentences.en: But shortly after the journey began, he vanished without a trace, leaving behind a mystery that would captivate the world for decades.
sentences.zh: 但就在旅程开始后不久，他便人间蒸发、杳无音讯，留下了一个让全世界着迷数十年的谜团。

sentences.en: You might remember this story from episode 525, the one on Legendary Lost Cities and Civilisations, which came out earlier this year, where we told the story of Fawcett within the context of stories about Atlantis and El Dorado.
sentences.zh: 你可能从今年早些时候播出的第 525 期节目《传说中的失落之城与文明》中听过这个故事，我们在节目中将 Fawcett 的故事与亚特兰蒂斯和 El Dorado 的传说结合在了一起。

sentences.en: Now, the stories of Atlantis and El Dorado deserve their own standalone episodes too, but today, it is time for Percy Harrison Fawcett.
sentences.zh: 当然，亚特兰蒂斯和 El Dorado 的故事也同样值得单独做成节目，但今天，轮到 Percy Harrison Fawcett 了。

sentences.en: To understand how Fawcett came to risk everything for this mythical city, and most likely pay the ultimate price, we need to rewind to the earliest chapters of his life.
sentences.zh: 要理解 Fawcett 为什么会为了这座神秘的城市押上一切，并很可能付出了生命的代价，我们需要回溯他生命中最早的那些章节。

sentences.en: Let’s start there: with a young man born into a world that seemed to breed explorers as readily as it did aristocrats, often with a very fuzzy line between the two, which was the case of Percy Harrison Fawcett.
sentences.zh: 让我们从那里开始：一个年轻人出生在一个似乎和贵族一样盛产探险家的世界里，而且这两者之间的界限往往非常模糊，Percy Harrison Fawcett 就是这种情况。

sentences.en: He was born in 1867 into a well-to-do British family, Yorkshire gentry that had made a lot of money in shipping in the early days of the British empire.
sentences.zh: 他于 1867 年出生于一个富裕的英国家庭，属于约克郡乡绅阶层，其家族在英帝国早期通过航运业赚取了巨额财富。

sentences.en: His father was something of a free spirit—an adventurer, a friend to literary figures, and a bit of a gambler.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲有点像个自由灵魂——一个冒险家、文学界名流的朋友，还带点赌徒气质。

sentences.en: It was the sort of life one could lead in Victorian England, at least if you were born into a wealthy, aristocratic family.
sentences.zh: 这正是维多利亚时代的人可以过上的生活，至少如果你出生在一个富有的贵族家庭的话。

sentences.en: There was little concern for “work” in our modern understanding of the word, and such families would live off large inheritances passed down from generation to generation.
sentences.zh: 当时人们对我们现在理解意义上的“工作”并没有太多概念，这样的家庭单靠代代相传的巨额遗产就能过活。

sentences.en: So, what did you do as a Victorian aristocrat?
sentences.zh: 那么，作为一个维多利亚时代的贵族，你会做什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, you could, of course, sit around playing cards, drinking port, and gambling your family’s fortune away, as it seemed Percy Fawcett’s father did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你当然可以闲坐着打牌、喝波特酒，把家族的财富挥霍一空，看起来 Percy Fawcett 的父亲就是这么做的。

sentences.en: But you could also develop other interests, and for some, this took the form of a fascination with distant corners of the globe.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以培养其他兴趣，对某些人来说，这种兴趣表现为对地球遥远角落的迷恋。

sentences.en: Britain was still riding the wave of empire, funding expeditions to map and claim territories on nearly every continent, and men who had the nerve for it were in high demand.
sentences.zh: 英国当时仍乘着帝国的浪潮，资助远征队去绘制和宣示几乎每个大洲的领土主权，而那些有胆量的人正是炙手可热的香饽饽。

sentences.en: Percy Fawcett would find himself to be one of these men.
sentences.zh: Percy Fawcett 发现自己就是这样的人。

sentences.en: At the age of 17, he was sent to The Royal Military Academy at Woolwich, where he reportedly learned “to regard the risk of death as the most piquant sauce to life”.
sentences.zh: 17 岁时，他被送往位于伍尔维克的皇家军事学院，据报道，他在那里学会了“把面临死亡的风险当作生活最够味的点缀”。

sentences.en: After graduating, he was commissioned into the Royal Artillery.
sentences.zh: 毕业后，他被委任为皇家炮兵少尉。

sentences.en: But he quickly discovered that his talents lay beyond conventional soldiering.
sentences.zh: 但他很快发现，自己的才能并不在常规的军旅生涯中。

sentences.en: He had a knack for languages and a taste for the exotic.
sentences.zh: 他很有语言天赋，并且对异国风情充满兴趣。

sentences.en: He spent time in Ceylon, modern-day Sri Lanka, Hong Kong, and Malta, and also spent time working as a British spy in North Africa, all by his mid-30s, I should add.
sentences.zh: 我在补充一句，他曾在锡兰（也就是如今的斯里兰卡）、香港和马耳他生活过，还曾在北非担任过英国间谍，这些都是他在 30 岁出头之前经历的。

sentences.en: This sense of adventure and a clear talent for existing outside his comfort zone almost magnetically drew him to an organisation called the Royal Geographical Society.
sentences.zh: 这种冒险精神以及在舒适区之外生存的明显天赋，像磁铁一样将他吸引到了一个名为皇家地理学会的组织。

sentences.en: Now, if you look at the Royal Geographical Society’s website today, you’ll find that it claims to be “the UK's learned society and professional body for geography”.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你今天去浏览皇家地理学会的网站，你会发现它自称是“英国地理学界的学术社团和专业机构”。

sentences.en: Unless you have a particular passion for geography, this might not sound like the most interesting club in the world.
sentences.zh: 除非你对地理有着特殊的热情，否则这听起来可能不是世界上最有趣的俱乐部。

sentences.en: But 150 years ago, it was in the business of “creating” geography, of sponsoring and supporting expeditions to explore, map and understand the natural world.
sentences.zh: 但在 150 年前，它的核心业务是“创造”地理，即赞助和支持旨在探索、绘制并了解自然世界的远征活动。

sentences.en: It raised money for expeditions in previously uncharted territory and supported the missions of many of the explorers we’ve talked about before on this show: David Livingstone’s African missions, Scott and Shackleton’s missions to reach the South Pole, and, of course, the research of Charles Darwin.
sentences.zh: 它为前往先前未出道领土的远征筹集资金，并支持了我们在本节目中多次谈到的许多探险家的任务：大卫·利文斯顿的非洲任务、斯科特和沙克尔顿征服南极的远征，当然，还有查尔斯·达尔文的研究。

sentences.en: For a young man keen on adventure and with a high tolerance for risk, it was a natural home.
sentences.zh: 对于一个渴望冒险且风险承受能力极高的年轻人来说，这里是个天然的归宿。

sentences.en: The Royal Geographical Society had its sights set on South America and proposed this as an option to Fawcett.
sentences.zh: 皇家地理学会将目光投向了南美洲，并向 Fawcett 提出了这个选项。

sentences.en: At the time, large parts of Bolivia, Peru, and Brazil were practically unmapped in the eyes of European powers, who were eager to define borders and exploit the land’s resources.
sentences.zh: 当时，在欧洲列强眼中，玻利维亚、秘鲁和巴西的大片地区实际上仍是未标绘的空白，而他们正急于划定边界并掠夺这片土地的资源。

sentences.en: Fawcett was told by the president of the Society that, and I’m quoting directly, “the terrain was all but impassable, it would take up two years and there was no guarantee of survival.”
sentences.zh: 学会会长对 Fawcett 说，我在这里直接引述原话，“那里的地形几乎无法通行，需要耗时两年，而且无法保证能活下来。”

sentences.en: What’s more, “disease was rampant, and the local Indians who had been brutally and mercilessly attacked by the rubber trappers would kill interlopers on sight.”
sentences.zh: 更不用说，“疾病横行，当地印第安人曾遭到橡胶采伐者的残酷无情袭击，见到外来者就会格杀勿论。”

sentences.en: This was, by the way, at the height of the rubber boom, so what the president of the society was referring to was the fact that native tribes were now so used to outsiders encroaching on their territory and trying to claim it for themselves that outsiders would typically be greeted by a storm of poison darts and arrows.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，当时正值橡胶热潮的顶峰，所以学会会长所指的是这样一种情况：当地部落已经对外界侵入其领地并试图据为己有的行为习以为常，因此外来者通常会遭到毒镖和毒箭的狂轰滥炸。

sentences.en: They were not given a warm welcome. So, given all of this, was Fawcett interested in the job?
sentences.zh: 他们并没有受到热烈欢迎。那么，鉴于这一切，Fawcett 对这份工作感兴趣吗？

sentences.en: Interested? He thought it was his life’s calling.
sentences.zh: 感兴趣？他认为这是他一生的使命。

sentences.en: It was what he had been put on this Earth to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是他被派到这个世界上要做的事。

sentences.en: His first mission was in 1906, and he amazed everyone by returning intact and a year ahead of schedule.
sentences.zh: 他的第一次任务是在 1906 年，他毫发无伤地归来，并且比预定时间提前了一年，这让所有人惊叹不已。

sentences.en: Not only had he managed it, but he had got the bug, he loved every minute of it, and as soon as he returned to London, he wanted to go straight back.
sentences.zh: 他不仅成功完成了任务，而且还上了瘾，他热爱其中的每一分钟，一回到伦敦就迫不及待地想马上回去。

sentences.en: It didn’t take long for his fame to grow, and he became renowned for his skill in surveying these rugged, remote regions.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，他的名气越来越大，并因擅长勘测这些险峻偏远的地区而闻名遐迩。

sentences.en: He'd tramp through mosquito infested jungles with bundles of maps and a theodolite, a type of instrument used for surveying territory and measuring angles.
sentences.zh: 他会背着一捆捆地图和经纬仪——一种用于勘测地形和测量角度的仪器，跋涉在蚊虫肆虐的丛林中。

sentences.en: Undeterred by this incredibly hostile territory, he would calmly record latitudes and longitudes in areas where few outsiders had ever ventured.
sentences.zh: 在这片极其恶劣的土地上，他毫不气馁，在极少有外来者涉足的地区冷静地记录着经纬度。

sentences.en: And with every mission he went on, slowly but surely, more areas of the map would get filled in.
sentences.zh: 随着他每一次任务的执行，地图上的空白区域缓慢而坚定地被一点点填满。

sentences.en: And stories of his exploits spread quickly.
sentences.zh: 他英勇事迹的故事迅速流传开来。

sentences.en: He claimed to have shot enormous 20-metre-long anacondas, to have encountered tribes that no other European had seen, and to have a near-superhuman resistance to the fevers and diseases that ravaged his fellow explorers.
sentences.zh: 他声称自己射杀过长达 20 米的巨大森蚺，遇到过其他欧洲人从未见过的部落，并且对折磨同行探险家的热病和疾病具有近乎超人的抵抗力。

sentences.en: Other men would get struck down within days or even hours of setting foot into the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 其他人一踏入亚马逊，几天甚至几小时内就会被击倒。

sentences.en: They would be consumed by flesh-eating maggots or larvae, they would be blinded by little worms, there were all manner of diseases and threats that killed or crippled his travelling companions.
sentences.zh: 他们会被食肉蛆虫或幼虫侵蚀，会被小虫子弄瞎双眼，有各种各样的疾病和威胁杀死了或致残了他的同伴。

sentences.en: But not Fawcett. For some reason, he simply didn’t get ill, or at least never seriously ill.
sentences.zh: 但 Fawcett 没有。不知为什么，他就是不会生病，或者至少从未生过重病。

sentences.en: He also seemed never to tire. When the going got tough, and his party hadn’t eaten for several days or someone was suffering from a disease, he wouldn’t let them lie down to rest.
sentences.zh: 他似乎也从不知疲倦。当情况变得艰难，他的队伍已经好几天没吃东西，或者有人生病时，他绝不允许他们躺下休息。

sentences.en: Lying down was giving up, he knew that every time a sick or tired man lay down to rest, it was harder to get back up again.
sentences.zh: 躺下就等于放弃，他深知，一个生病或疲惫的人每一次躺下休息，想要再次站起来就会变得更加困难。

sentences.en: If you died, Fawcett said, you died standing up.
sentences.zh: Fawcett 说，如果你要死，那就站着死。

sentences.en: Some believed he exaggerated his exploits for fame, but many saw him as the real deal—a man born to explore.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为他为了出名而夸大了自己的战绩，但许多人视他为货真价实的传奇——一个天生为探索而生的人。

sentences.en: As was the norm with Victorian explorers, he recorded everything in a diary, and published it on his return.
sentences.zh: 正如维多利亚时代探险家的常态一样，他在日记中记录了一切，并在归来后将其出版。

sentences.en: With every new publication his fame grew, and while he was away on a mission, Victorian England awaited his return and the tales of mystery and adventure that he would come back with.
sentences.zh: 随着每一本新书的出版，他的名气水涨船高，而在他外出执行任务期间，维多利亚时代的英国都在翘首以盼他的归来，等待他带回那些充满神秘与冒险的故事。

sentences.en: Along the way, there were rumours that he had never really left the secret service, and that he was still working as a British spy.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，有传言称他从未真正离开过秘密情报局，并且仍在为英国担任间谍。

sentences.en: Mapping distant frontiers, after all, was often as politically useful as it was scientifically exciting.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，绘制遥远边疆的地图通常在政治上和在科学上一样有用。

sentences.en: Yet for Fawcett, there seemed to be something more profound than mere mapmaking.
sentences.zh: 然而对 Fawcett 来说，似乎有一种比单纯绘制地图更深刻的东西。

sentences.en: In his conversations with indigenous communities, he heard tales of a great city hidden far into the rainforest, a place filled with monumental architecture and advanced culture.
sentences.zh: 在与土著社区的交谈中，他听到了一些传说：在雨林深处隐藏着一座伟大的城市，那里有宏伟的建筑和先进的文化。

sentences.en: Local lore described it in hushed tones —this was no simple village of huts, but something far older, far grander.
sentences.zh: 当地的传说低声描述着它——这不是一个简单的茅草村落，而是某种更加古老、更加宏伟的东西。

sentences.en: It initially seemed like folklore, a tale passed down through generations, but then he found it mentioned in a manuscript in the National Library in Rio de Janeiro.
sentences.zh: 起初这听口音像是民间传说，是代代相传的故事，但随后他在里约热内卢国家图书馆的一份手稿中发现了它的记载。

sentences.en: The more he looked, the more clues seemed to point to the existence of this city he called Z.
sentences.zh: 他越是深入寻找，似乎就有越多的线索指向这座他称之为 Z 的城市。

sentences.en: And, what’s more, Machu Picchu was discovered high in the hills of Peru in 1911.
sentences.zh: 而且，更重要的是，1911 年在秘鲁的高山中发现了马丘比丘。

sentences.en: Fawcett took this as yet more evidence that the jungles and mountains of South America held secrets that were yet to be discovered.
sentences.zh: Fawcett 将此视为又一证据，证明南美洲的丛林和山脉隐藏着尚未被发现的秘密。

sentences.en: And somewhere, deep in the Amazon, was Z.
sentences.zh: 而在亚马逊深处的某个地方，正藏着 Z。

sentences.en: He became convinced that if he could find such a city, it would rewrite what the world believed about human civilisation in the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 他坚信，如果自己能找到这样一座城市，将会彻底改写世人对亚马逊人类文明的认知。

sentences.en: Now, this was in the early 20th century, and just as his obsession was reaching a fever pitch, Europe descended into the chaos of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 当时正值 20 世纪初，正当他对这件事的痴迷达到狂热顶点时，欧洲陷入了一战的混乱之中。

sentences.en: Fawcett at this time was nearly fifty years old, hardly the age at which one typically enlists for frontline service.
sentences.zh: 当时的 Fawcett 已经快五十岁了，这绝不是通常人们会应征参军上前线的年纪。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, he had a deep sense of patriotism, he had extensive military and leadership experience, and he believed his country needed him.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他有着强烈的爱国主义精神，拥有丰富的军事和领导经验，并且他相信祖国需要他。

sentences.en: He was probably right. He returned to Britain, traded his machete and compass for an officer’s uniform, and headed into the trenches of northern France.
sentences.zh: 他可能没想错。他返回英国，脱下砍刀和指南针，换上军官制服，一头扎进了法国北部战壕的泥潭中。

sentences.en: The horrors he witnessed there changed him forever.
sentences.zh: 他在那里亲眼目睹的人间地狱彻底改变了他。

sentences.en: Young men—boys, really—were being sent “over the top” into a maelstrom of machine-gun fire, poison gas, and artillery barrages.
sentences.zh: 年轻人——其实还是些男孩——被派去“冲锋陷阵”，卷入机枪扫射、毒气和炮火交织的暴风雨中。

sentences.en: It was a grim lesson in how “civilised” nations could turn technology and organisation into instruments of mass destruction.
sentences.zh: 这是一次残酷的教训，让他们看清了“文明”国家如何将技术和组织变成大规模毁灭的工具。

sentences.en: Amid the mud, blood, and sheer senselessness of it all, Fawcett began to question the supposed superiority of Western progress.
sentences.zh: 在一片泥泞、血腥和毫无意义的混乱之中，Fawcett 开始质疑西方进步所谓的优越性。

sentences.en: If this was what civilisation had to offer, was it truly more advanced than the tribal societies he had encountered in the Amazon?
sentences.zh: 如果这就是文明所能提供的一切，它真的比他在亚马逊遇到的那些部落社会更先进吗？

sentences.en: During those long, haunted nights on the Western Front, his mind drifted back to the lush green canopy of South America, to the gentle currents of unknown rivers, and to the stories of that hidden city.
sentences.zh: 在西线战场那些漫长而挥之不去的夜晚里，他的思绪飘回了南美洲郁郁葱葱的绿色树冠、不知名河流的柔和水流，以及关于那座隐藏城市的种种传说。

sentences.en: Perhaps, he mused, the true measure of civilisation wasn’t bombs and factories, and industrial output, but wisdom and harmony—qualities that might lie undiscovered beneath the rainforest’s thick foliage.
sentences.zh: 他沉思着，或许文明真正的标尺不是炸弹、工厂和工业产出，而是智慧与和谐——这些品质或许正静静地躺在雨林厚重枝叶下，等待着被发掘。

sentences.en: Unlike a large proportion of the young men he commanded, Fawcett survived the Somme.
sentences.zh: 与他麾下的大多数年轻人不同，Fawcett 在索姆河战役中活了下来。

sentences.en: And when the war ended, he wasted no time returning to his life’s mission.
sentences.zh: 战争一结束，他便毫不耽搁地回到了自己一生的使命中。

sentences.en: Now in his late fifties, hardly an age most men would choose to slog through dense undergrowth in searing heat, he was more determined than ever.
sentences.zh: 此时他已年近六旬，这绝不是大多数人会选择在酷热中艰难穿行于密林灌木丛中的年纪，但他却比以往任何时候都更加坚定。

sentences.en: He returned, first in 1920, but the mission was a failure.
sentences.zh: 他再次出发，最初是在 1920 年，但那次任务以失败告终。

sentences.en: Bad weather conspired against him, and the now 53-year-old wasn’t quite as young and nimble as he had been 15 years before.
sentences.zh: 恶劣的天气与他作对，而且此时年过五三的他也远不如 15 年前那样年轻敏捷了。

sentences.en: Plus, his legendary resistance to tropical disease seemed to be weakening.
sentences.zh: 此外，他那对热带疾病的传奇抵抗力似乎也在减弱。

sentences.en: He fell ill, too ill to continue the mission, and had to return to England.
sentences.zh: 他病倒了，病得无法继续任务，不得不返回英国。

sentences.en: But if you had thought this would have been enough to put him off for life, well, you would be wrong.
sentences.zh: 但如果你以为这就足以让他打消终生探索的念头，那你就大错特错了。

sentences.en: For Fawcett this was a temporary setback, and he soon started planning another mission.
sentences.zh: 对 Fawcett 来说，这只是暂时的挫折，他很快就开始筹划另一次任务。

sentences.en: The problem was that he didn’t have the money to do it.
sentences.zh: 问题在于他没有资金来支持这一切。

sentences.en: Although he was what we would probably call a celebrity explorer by this point, he didn’t find it easy to find anyone willing to pay for the trip.
sentences.zh: 尽管到这个时候他可以说是家喻户晓的明星探险家，但他发现很难找到愿意为这次旅行出资的人。

sentences.en: The Royal Geographical Society had mixed feelings about further expeditions; by then, Fawcett had a reputation as something of a maverick, difficult to control, and past his prime as an Amazonian explorer.
sentences.zh: 皇家地理学会对进一步的远征态度复杂；到那时，Fawcett 在人们眼中已经有点特立独行、难以管教，而且作为亚马逊探险家已经过了巅峰期。

sentences.en: Yet he managed it. He managed to secure just enough funding, some from newspaper deals and some from private backers, to return to the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 然而他还是做到了。他设法筹集到了刚刚够用的资金，一部分来自报社的交易，一部分来自私人赞助商，从而得以重返亚马逊。

sentences.en: His plan was straightforward and audacious: travel into uncharted territory, gather fresh evidence, and come out triumphant—maybe with gold, maybe with tales of a living civilisation beyond the scope of imagination.
sentences.zh: 他的计划直接而大胆：深入未知的领土，收集新的证据，然后凯旋而归——也许带着黄金，也许带着超越想象力的活文明的故事。

sentences.en: Some people called him delusional; others saw him as a visionary.
sentences.zh: 有人说他得了妄想症；也有人视他为有远见的梦想家。

sentences.en: Fawcett himself was unwavering, but he decided not to make the journey alone.
sentences.zh: Fawcett 本人坚定不移，但他决定不独自踏上这段旅程。

sentences.en: He recruited his son, Jack, along with Jack’s friend, a young man named Raleigh Rimell.
sentences.zh: 他招募了他的儿子 Jack，以及 Jack 的朋友、一个名叫 Raleigh Rimell 的年轻人。

sentences.en: They set off in 1925, going up rivers, cutting through dense jungle, and negotiating passage with tribes that had rarely, if ever— encountered outsiders.
sentences.zh: 他们在 1925 年出发，逆流而上，劈开密林，并与那些极少——甚至从未——接触过外来者的部落进行交涉。

sentences.en: For a while, all went well. Fawcett sent intermittent updates via runners who carried letters back to the edges of the jungle, where telegraphs could relay his words to the wider world.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，一切都很顺利。Fawcett 通过信使断断续续地发回消息，信使将信件带到丛林边缘，再由电报将他的话语传送到更广阔的世界。

sentences.en: He sounded enthusiastic, confident, even.
sentences.zh: 他的语气听起来热情洋溢、自信满满，甚至可以说是意气风发。

sentences.en: Soon, though, the messages stopped. In his last known letter, written about a month into the journey, Fawcett described how they were about to push into completely uncharted territory.
sentences.zh: 然而很快，消息就断了。在他已知的最后一封信中，大约写于行程开始一个月后，Fawcett 描述了他们即将深入完全未知的领土。

sentences.en: After that point, nothing more was heard.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，就再也没有任何音讯了。

sentences.en: He, Jack, and Rimell effectively vanished.
sentences.zh: 他和 Jack 以及 Rimell 实际上就这样人间蒸发了。

sentences.en: No one knows exactly what happened. Some guess they succumbed to disease or starvation.
sentences.zh: 没有人确切知道发生了什么。有人猜测他们死于疾病或饥饿。

sentences.en: Others suspect they ran afoul of a hostile tribe.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则怀疑他们撞上了敌对的部落。

sentences.en: A few spin wilder theories: that Fawcett discovered Z, decided to stay, and purposefully vanished from Western civilisation.
sentences.zh: 还有少数人脑洞大开：认为 Fawcett 找到了 Z，决定留下来，并故意从西方文明中隐匿了。

sentences.en: Their disappearance ignited a feverish obsession.
sentences.zh: 他们的失踪引发了一种狂热的痴迷。

sentences.en: Adventurers from around the globe tried to retrace Fawcett’s steps.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的冒险家都试图重走 Fawcett 的足迹。

sentences.en: And many didn’t make it out of the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 但许多人没能活着离开亚马逊。

sentences.en: An estimated 100 explorers died or disappeared themselves in the search for the British trio, so many that by the 1930s, the Brazilian government banned further attempts to find him, fearing the toll on human life.
sentences.zh: 据估计，在寻找这三名英国人的过程中，有多达 100 名探险家丧生或失踪，人数如此之多，以至于到了 20 世纪 30 年代，巴西政府出于对人命损失的担忧，禁止了进一步寻找他的尝试。

sentences.en: And over the decades, rumours spread: bones were found here or there, or a tribe told stories of a tall white-haired stranger.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几十年里，各种传言四处散播：这里或那里发现了骨头，或者某个部落讲述了关于一个身材高大、白发苍苍的陌生人的故事。

sentences.en: But no definitive proof of Fawcett’s fate has ever come to light.
sentences.zh: 但始终没有任何确凿的证据来证明 Fawcett 的最终命运。

sentences.en: Despite the countless expeditions launched to uncover the truth, Fawcett’s remains have never been identified.
sentences.zh: 尽管为了揭开真相发起了无数次远征，Fawcett 的遗骸却从未被确认过。

sentences.en: Whatever happened to him, the Amazon has guarded her secrets well.
sentences.zh: 无论他身上发生了什么，亚马逊都把自己的秘密守护得很好。

sentences.en: And, in a sense, Fawcett’s obsession may not have been in vain.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，Fawcett 的执念或许并非徒劳。

sentences.en: He might have been right. Recent archaeological studies have revealed that parts of the Amazon once supported large, complex societies, lending credibility to the idea that advanced civilisations could exist there, hidden from outside eyes.
sentences.zh: 他是对的。最近的考古研究表明，亚马逊的部分地区曾经养育过庞大而复杂的社会，这为“那里可能存在不为外人所知的先进文明”这一观点增添了可信度。

sentences.en: Though Fawcett never returned to prove the existence of “Z,” his conviction that the region was more than just a green desert was remarkably prescient.
sentences.zh: 尽管 Fawcett 从未归来以证明“Z”的存在，但他坚信该地区不仅仅是一片绿色荒漠，这种看法具有非凡的先见之明。

sentences.en: Today, Percy Fawcett is often called “the real-life Indiana Jones,” a moniker that suits his larger-than-life persona and daring exploits.
sentences.zh: 如今，Percy Fawcett 常被称为“现实版的 Indiana Jones”，这个绰号非常符合他传奇般的人物性格和惊险刺激的壮举。

sentences.en: Clearly, he was a fascinating character but was full of contradictions.
sentences.zh: 很显然，他是一个迷人却又充满矛盾的人物。

sentences.en: An imperial agent but an open-minded explorer.
sentences.zh: 他既是帝国的代理人，又是思想开明的探险家。

sentences.en: A Victorian aristocrat, but one who started to question the superiority of European civilisation.
sentences.zh: 他是个维多利亚时代的贵族，却又开始质疑欧洲文明的优越性。

sentences.en: An apparently loving husband and father, but one who took his oldest son to his death.
sentences.zh: 他表面上是个慈爱的丈夫和父亲，却带着自己的大儿子走向了死亡。

sentences.en: A man who knew full-well that he might not return from the mission, but went anyway.
sentences.zh: 他明明知道自己可能无法从任务中活着回来，却还是毅然前往。

sentences.en: So, let me leave you with a quote widely attributed to Percy Fawcett, which seems to sum up his attitude rather well.
sentences.zh: 因此，我想留给各位一句广泛认为是 Percy Fawcett 所说的话，这句话似乎很好地总结了他的态度。

sentences.en: “It should be remembered that the difficulties are great and the tale of disasters a long one, for the few remaining unknown corners of the world exact a price for their secrets.”
sentences.zh: “应该记住，困难是巨大的，灾难的故事也很长，因为世界上仅存的几个未知角落要为它们的秘密索取代价。”

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on Percy Harrison Fawcett, a man I hope you will agree most certainly deserves the title of a real-life Indiana Jones.
sentences.zh: 好了，这就是今天关于 Percy Harrison Fawcett 的全部内容，我相信大家都会同意，他绝对当得起现实版 Indiana Jones 的称号。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目对你有所帮助，并且让你学到了新东西。

sentences.en: I think these ones on Adventurers are some of the most fun episodes we make, and if you’d like to listen to more of them, then we have that one on Atlantis and El Dorado, that’s episode number 525, but we also have a bunch more.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这些关于冒险家的节目是我们制作的最有趣的节目之一，如果你想听更多类似的内容，我们有关于亚特兰蒂斯和 El Dorado 的那一期，那是第 525 期，不过我们还有很多其他的。

sentences.en: From attempts to find the north and south poles to a three-part mini-series on the search for the source of the Nile, we've got loads that you might not have listened to yet.
sentences.zh: 从寻找南极和北极的尝试，到关于寻找尼罗河源头的三集迷你剧，我们有很多你可能还没听过的节目。

sentences.en: The easiest way to find them is probably on our website, where you can search for episodes with the tag “adventure” or “exploration”.
sentences.zh: 找到它们的最好方法可能是在我们的网站上，你可以在那里搜索带有标签“adventure”或“exploration”的节目。

sentences.en: I’ll put a link in the description so you can just click on that and go straight there.
sentences.zh: 我会在简介里放一个链接，这样你只要点一下就能直接过去了。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你刚才收听的是由 Leonardo English 推出的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请多保重，我们下期节目见。
